pcs.pc_description: Express the epidemiology of trauma
Describe the overview of Trauma Care Systems in our country
Ensure well-being of trauma care team
Ensure protection of victims and bystanders in an emergency scene
Ensure personal safety at all times
Manage any kind of violence or civil disturbances at the scene
Manage mass casualty incident
Acquire basic knowledge of the structure of human body in the context of pre-hospital trauma care
Implement the knowledge of anatomy in common emergency conditions
Acquire basic knowledge about various physiological functions of individual systems in the human body

• Conduct examination and observation of the following aspects: • • General appearance, mental and emotional status • • Physique, built and nutritional status • • Facial expression and speech • • Eyes, skin, feet, neck • • Lymph nodes, pallor, icterus, edema, cynosis, nails, hair etc. • • Pupillary examination including reflexes
Conduct clinical examination of the respiratory system: Inspection, palpation, percussion and auscultation of the respiratory system
Conduct clinical examination of the cardiovascular system: Pulse, BP, Precordium
Record body temperature
Conduct sensory system examination and motor system examination

Acquire basic information about the drugs (including their adverse effects), relevant to trauma care that may be used while transporting the patient from the accident site to the healthcare facility / trauma care facility
Demonstrate usage of various emergency drugs
Demonstrate usage of various types of IV fluids
Demonstrate preparation of the IV drip
Demonstrate various sterilization and disinfection techniques of ambulance and hospital equipment and procedures
Demonstrate donning, doffing and discarding of personal protective equipment (PPE)
Demonstrate sample collection techniques in correct containers
Follow infection control guidelines and biomedical waste management procedures
Apply information on infectious diseases, various sterilization techniques, concept of wound infections, biomedical waste and occupational exposures in the pre-hospital trauma care
Keep oneself updated with the legal and ethical issues concerning professional practice and aspects on notifications and documentation related to Pre-hospital Trauma care
Demonstrate documentation of report, recording of findings using MLC case records, Post-mortem reports, Age reports
Demonstrate care of various types of injuries using various museum specimens and weapons
Identify medico-legal aspects of injuries
Demonstrate practical medico-legal aspects of asphyxia cases like preservation of knot of ligature material etc.
